English: Simple Reliquary
A humble wooden chest kept near the altar, providing the first secure storage for sacred relics, watched over by the temples clergy.
Stone Reliquary Alcove
A modest alcove built from stone within the temple walls, offering better protection for relics and attracting local pilgrims.
Guarded Reliquary Room
A small, locked chamber with iron-bound doors and regular night vigils, ensuring the relics are safe from theft and desecration.
Vaulted Reliquary
A strong, stone-vaulted chamber deep within the temple, requiring advanced construction techniques, with ornate ironwork and elaborate locks.
Reinforced Reliquary
A reliquary chamber with steel reinforcements, secret compartments, and a permanent roster of temple guards, making it nearly impervious to intrusion.
Reliquary Treasury
A grand treasury built to both display and safeguard relics, attracting pilgrims and increasing temple wealth, with a dedicated staff of clerics and guards.
Blessed Reliquary Hall
A sanctified hall, richly decorated and blessed by high-ranking clergy, drawing the devout from far and wide and cementing the temples spiritual influence.
Golden Reliquary Chamber
Walls gilded with gold leaf, this chamber is both a testament to faith and a fortress for holy relics, inspiring awe and reverence among all who enter.
Jeweled Reliquary Vault
A vault adorned with gemstones and rare marbles, its opulence draws the faithful and the powerful, serving as both sanctuary and unbreakable stronghold.
Sanctified Reliquary Sanctuary
The holiest sanctuary, consecrated by the highest religious authorities, with relics displayed behind crystal and gold, protected by elite guards and sacred rites.
